title: The affine torsion cohomological dimension bound
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $c\ge0$ an integer with $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\le c$. For any nonempty affine finite-type $K$-scheme $X$,
$$\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X)\le\dim X+c,$$
with bounds understood as in [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] and Krull dimension as in [def-kun-dimension]. If $X$ is empty, $H^q(X,F)=0$ for every torsion abelian etale sheaf $F$ and every $q\ge0$.

proof.text: Throughout, torsion means that every local section is locally killed by some positive integer; no single integer need annihilate the sheaf. The cohomology is ordinary derived-section cohomology on the small etale site, and a field bound is the corresponding bound on its affine spectrum. We prove, by strong induction on the nonnegative integer $d$, the asserted bound for every nonempty affine finite-type scheme of dimension at most $d$, simultaneously over all fields and all available field bounds $c$. The empty scheme has zero section functor and hence zero cohomology. Finite dimension follows from Noether normalization and its dimension assertion. Algebraic extension of the ground field preserves the dimension of each affine coordinate ring. Thus after establishing the bound $d$ over algebraically closed fields in dimension $d$, the ground-field comparison gives $d+c$ over every field; this descent is made at each induction stage, before advancing to $d+1$. An algebraically closed field is separably closed and has torsion bound zero.

We will repeatedly use the following consequence for a finite morphism $u:T\to S$. Apply $u_*$ to an injective resolution of an abelian sheaf $A$. Exactness makes this a resolution of $u_*A$, and preservation of injectives makes it an injective resolution. Since $\Gamma(S,u_*I)=\Gamma(T,I)$ termwise, $H^r(T,A)=H^r(S,u_*A)$ for every $r$. The finite-stalk product formula shows that $u_*A$ is torsion when $A$ is torsion, and is killed by $n$ when $A$ is killed by $n$: a finite tuple of torsion elements has a common annihilator.

source.place: Proof, exact finite direct image reductions

proof.text: For $d=0$, Noether normalization makes the structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ finite, so the preceding finite comparison proves the bound $c$. For $d=1$ over an algebraically closed field the arbitrary-curve bound gives bound one, since the scheme is affine and therefore separated; the descent in step 1 proves the bound over all fields. Now fix $d>1$ and suppose all smaller dimensions have been proved over every field. If $\dim X<d$, the induction hypothesis already gives the required bound; hence assume $\dim X=d$. Work first over algebraically closed $K$. Noether normalization supplies a finite morphism $X\to\mathbf A_K^d$. The finite comparison reduces the problem to an arbitrary torsion sheaf $M$ on $\mathbf A_K^d$. Initially suppose $nM=0$ for one positive integer $n$.

Let $Y$ be smooth integral and finite type of dimension $d$ over $K$, let $D$ be an effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]), and write $j:Y\setminus D\to Y$. At $y\in D$ put $a=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(y)$, $R=\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{Y,\bar y}$, and choose the field $F\subset R$ supplied by the smooth strict-local field-model lemma. A local equation $h$ of $D$ is nonzero in the domain $R$ and belongs to its maximal ideal. For $P(T)\ne0$ in $F[T]$, write $P(T)=T^m(b+TQ(T))$ with $b\in F^\times$. Then $b+hQ(h)$ has nonzero residue, hence is a unit of $R$. Thus $P(h)$ is invertible in $R[1/h]$, and evaluation embeds $F(T)$ in $R[1/h]$. In particular $h$ is transcendental over $F$. If $z_1,\ldots,z_s$ are independent over $F(h)$, a purported nonzero relation $Q(h,z_1,\ldots,z_s)=0$ with $Q\in F[T,Z_1,\ldots,Z_s]$ can be written $\sum_{\alpha}Q_{\alpha}(h)z^{\alpha}=0$. At least one $Q_{\alpha}$ is a nonzero polynomial, so transcendence of $h$ makes its coefficient $Q_{\alpha}(h)$ nonzero. This is a nonzero polynomial relation over $F(h)$, a contradiction. Thus $h,z_1,\ldots,z_s$ are independent over $F$. Consequently $s+1\le d-a$. For every finitely generated $F(h)$-subalgebra $A\subset R[1/h]$, its fraction field is a subfield of $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, so the finite-type domain dimension formula gives $\dim A\le d-a-1<d$.

source.place: Proof, Local calculation in dimension d, algebraic calculation

proof.text: The finitely generated $F(h)$-subalgebras of $R[1/h]$ form a small filtered poset (the algebra generated by two of them dominates both), and their union is $R[1/h]$. Taking spectra gives an affine inverse-limit presentation with affine transition maps. The bound on $F(h)$ is one by the one-variable field lemma. The induction hypothesis, applicable over every field and in dimensions at most $d-a-1$, gives bound $d-a$ for each model. The affine-limit lemma therefore gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(\operatorname{Spec}R[1/h])\le d-a$. The strict-henselization stalk formula, applied to $j$, which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: locally on the target, an affine open where the Cartier ideal has generator $h$ has preimage the principal affine open $D(h)$, and an open immersion is separated, gives $(R^qj_*M)_{\bar y}=0$ whenever $q>d-a$.

source.place: Proof, Local calculation in dimension d, lower-dimensional induction and stalk formula

proof.text: Put $B=\mathbf A_K^{d-1}$, $Y=\mathbf P^1_K\times B$, $D=\{\infty\}\times B$, and let $j:\mathbf A_K^d\to Y$, $i:D\to Y$, $g:Y\to B$, and $f=gj$. These are the usual two polynomial charts of the projective line; in the chart at infinity $D$ has equation the last coordinate. Both polynomial charts of $Y$, and $B$ itself, are smooth over $K$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]; smoothness is local on the source. The chart coordinate rings are domains and their nonempty overlap is dense in each, so $Y$ is integral. In particular $Y$ has dimension $d$, and $\dim B=d-1$ (apply the finite-type domain dimension formula to the polynomial coordinate charts, whose variables are a transcendence basis). The projection $g$ is proper by properness of projective space. Etale restriction preserves injective resolutions, so restriction of $R^qj_*M$ to the open $\mathbf A^d$ is $R^q\mathrm{id}_*M=0$ for $q>0$. For any abelian etale sheaf $A$ supported on $D$, the unit $A\to i_*i^{-1}A$ is an isomorphism: off $D$ both stalks are zero, and on $D$ the finite-stalk formula and inverse-image stalk formula identify its stalk with the identity of $A_{\bar y}$. Geometric stalks detect isomorphisms. Apply this to write $R^qj_*M=i_*N_q$ for $q>0$.

source.place: Proof, From the local calculation to affine space, support on the infinity divisor

proof.text: For $N$ on $D$, an injective resolution $N\to I^\bullet$ stays an injective resolution under the exact functor $i_*$, which preserves injectives. Thus $R^pg_*(i_*N)$ is computed by $g_*i_*I^\bullet=(gi)_*I^\bullet$. Since $gi:D\to B$ is an isomorphism, this complex has no positive cohomology. Hence $R^pg_*R^qj_*M=0$ for $p>0,q>0$. All the sheaves here are killed by $n$: multiplication by $n$ on each derived functor value is the derived functor of $n\mathrm{id}_M=0$, by additivity.

source.place: Proof, From the local calculation to affine space, acyclicity on the boundary

proof.text: View $j_*M$ as a sheaf of $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$-modules. Apply the first, derived, assertion of finite-coefficient proper base change to $g$ and $(j_*M)[0]$; it applies to every object of $D^+$, with no finiteness or constructibility condition on the stalks. Forgetting coefficients commutes with derived direct image, including the structure morphism of each fibre. Its geometric fibres are projective lines over algebraically closed fields. The projective-line dimension bound and the arbitrary-curve lemma give zero fibre cohomology for $p>2$. The base-change isomorphism and geometric stalk conservativity imply $R^pg_*j_*M=0$ for $p>2$.

source.place: Proof, From the local calculation to affine space, proper projection

proof.text: Direct images preserve injectives, so the Grothendieck spectral sequence applies to $j_*$ followed by $g_*$. On its $E_2$ page the only possibly nonzero positions are the column $p=0$ and the row $q=0$ with $p\le2$. In total degree $r>2$, the term $(0,r)$ survives and is the only graded piece of the abutment: for $2\le\ell\le r$ the outgoing differential $d_{\ell}$ targets $(\ell,r-\ell+1)$, where both coordinates are positive; for $\ell=r+1$ it targets the zero term $(r+1,0)$; later targets have negative second coordinate. Incoming differentials would start in a negative first coordinate. Thus $R^rf_*M\cong g_*R^rj_*M$ for $r>2$. Write $v=gi:D\xrightarrow{\sim}B$. The boundary identification of step 6 gives $g_*R^rj_*M=g_*i_*N_r=v_*N_r$. At a geometric point $\bar z$ of $B$, the finite-stalk formula for the isomorphism $v$ identifies $(v_*N_r)_{\bar z}$ with $(N_r)_{v^{-1}\bar z}$. The inverse-image stalk formula identifies this with $(R^rj_*M)_{i v^{-1}\bar z}$. For $z\in B$ with $a=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(z)>d-r$, the local calculation at the corresponding point of $D$ gives a zero stalk. Hence $R^rf_*M$ has zero stalks at those points.

source.place: Proof, From the local calculation to affine space, spectral sequence and support bound for q>2

proof.text: For $r=2$, let $\eta$ be the generic point of $B$. The field-model lemma applied to $B$, where $a=\dim B=d-1$, says that its strict henselization is a regular local domain of dimension zero, with residue field $\kappa(\eta)^{\rm sep}$. A zero-dimensional regular local ring has maximal ideal generated by zero elements, and so is that residue field. The strict-henselization stalk formula for the affine projection $f$ therefore identifies the generic stalk of $R^2f_*M$ with $H^2(\mathbf A^1_{\kappa(\eta)^{\rm sep}},M|)$. By the dimension-one case, already established over every field, and torsion cohomological dimension zero of a separably closed field, this is zero. In the polynomial scheme $B$, the only point of residue transcendence degree $>d-2$ is its generic point: a nonzero prime gives a nonzero polynomial relation between the $d-1$ coordinate residues. Thus the same support bound holds for $r=2$.

source.place: Proof, From the local calculation to affine space, the exceptional degree q=2

proof.text: Let $N$ be a torsion sheaf on $B$ with zero stalks above transcendence degree $a\ge0$. The support-dimension-union lemma writes $N=\varinjlim_ZN_Z$ over closed $Z\subset B$ of dimension at most $a$. Equip $Z$ with its reduced closed subscheme structure. By the stalk argument in step 6, $N_Z=i_*i^{-1}N_Z$; by the finite comparison in step 2, $H^p(B,N_Z)=H^p(Z,i^{-1}N_Z)$. The scheme $Z$ is affine of finite type of dimension at most $a$. When $a<d$, induction over $K$ gives zero for $p>a$. Cohomology commutes with this filtered colimit on the qcqs scheme $B$, hence $H^p(B,N)=0$ for $p>a$. Apply this with $N=R^qf_*M$ and $a=d-q$ for $q\ge2$ and $a\ge0$. If $a<0$, steps 5 and 9 show every stalk vanishes, hence $N=0$. For $q=0,1$, induction on $B$ gives $H^p(B,R^qf_*M)=0$ for $p>d-1$.

source.place: Proof, Cohomology of the resulting sheaves on B

proof.text: Apply the Grothendieck spectral sequence to $f_*$ and $\Gamma(B,-)$; direct images preserve injectives, so the acyclicity hypothesis is satisfied. Its terms $H^p(B,R^qf_*M)$ vanish for $p+q>d$: for $q=0,1$ use $p\le d-1$, and for $q\ge2$ use $p\le d-q$. A first-quadrant convergent spectral sequence gives a finite filtration in each total degree, so the zero graded pieces force $H^r(\mathbf A^d,M)=0$ for $r>d$. Finally an arbitrary locally torsion $M$, without a uniform annihilator, is the filtered union of its subsheaves $M[n]$; each has just been treated, and cohomology commutes with this union. The finite comparison handles the original $X$, and the descent of step 1 completes the induction over all fields with bound $d+c$.

Exposed the strict-local coefficient-field input as one algebraic statement-only node; replaced the Kunneth-only point bound by the existing all-torsion bound. Added explicit finite-resolution comparison, closed-support stalk argument, coefficient-forgetting comparison and injective-preservation hypotheses; separated the exceptional generic degree-two calculation. Made the empty case explicit: the imported inequality has no meaning under the minus-infinity convention for empty Krull dimension, whereas the empty-site section functor is zero. All other quoted current statements still agree.
